q: Nutritional rickets is characterised by all EXCEPT:
e: Phosphate is low in nutritional rickets; high phosphate suggests CKD.

q: The earliest clinical sign of rickets in a 4-month-old is:
The X-ray sign of rickets at the wrist is:
o: Cupping and fraying of the metaphysis
e: Cupping, fraying and widening of the metaphysis.

q: Rickets with normal calcium, normal PTH and very low phosphate is:
e: Renal phosphate wasting; treat with phosphate + calcitriol.

q: A 6-month-old with rickets has a convulsion and calcium of 1.5 mmol/L. First treatment:
e: Hypocalcaemic fits: IV calcium gluconate slowly with ECG monitoring.
